target_customer: Colleges and universities that pay for a branded mobile app and engagement platform for students
problem: Students and institutions lacked one mobile place for campus resources, events and communication, which hurt engagement and persistence.
business_model: B2B SaaS annual and multi-year contracts per institution
product_category: Higher education mobile app and student engagement platform

founders.name: Danial Jameel
prior_employers: University of Toronto Student Life department
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (Jan 2017) says he worked in Student Life at the University of Toronto coordinating resources for about 15,000 incoming freshmen. Education not found.

founders.name: Alice Dinu
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as co-founder with a bio citing customer success, data strategy and M&A experience; the page claims a prior exit that is not verified.

founders.name: James Dang
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page, no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: A configurable campus app with integrations to LMS, events and directories is standard mobile engineering; the hard part was per-campus customization and integration at scale.

defensibility.rationale: TechCrunch reported two thirds of customers signed three year contracts upfront, and campus integrations create switching costs, but features were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it. The company merged with DubLabs in 2018 and then acquired Collabco, StuComm, AppScho (2021) and CampusGroups (2022) as consolidator.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Jan 2017) reported over 200 customers in 8 countries, profitability and multi-year contracts, showing institutions paid to improve student engagement.

branding.domain_note: Ready Education now uses readyeducation.com; the YC listing website referenced oohlalamobile.com

rebrands.why: Merger of OOHLALA Mobile and DubLabs into one company (Ready Education blog and CB Insights listing); naming reason not stated

brand_strength.rationale: B2B brand with little press about the brand itself; the OOHLALA name was retired in the 2018 merger. No sourced evidence of brand pull.

pivots.why: Merger to combine two higher education mobile platforms

outcome_analysis: Ready Education grew from OOHLALA Mobile, a profitable campus app startup with multi-year contracts, into a consolidator after the 2018 DubLabs merger and several acquisitions backed by Level Equity. It stayed active and raised modest early capital, which suggests a durable B2B subscription business rather than a venture style outlier.
notes: Series A reported as $4M by TechCrunch and EdSurge; a law firm announcement says $5.3M led by University Ventures (conflict). CB Insights lists a 2023 seed with Liquid 2 Ventures and an OOHLALA total of $4.14M, unverified aggregator figures. YC page says 350 institutions, a founder bio says 700. Competitors: none dated near the Summer 2016 batch were found (the 2015 EDUCAUSE review compares OOHLALA with unnamed alternatives), so the list is empty. Exit left as none: the 2018 event was a merger of OOHLALA and DubLabs, not a sale, and the company remains active. Founded year not stated in sources opened.
